questions.question: State the safe working practices for the headgear build, including the rules for saws, drills, knives and hot glue, for working at height and around the running winder, and the room habits.
questions.expected_answer: Dowel is sawn in a bench hook or clamp, never in the hand, with fingers behind the blade, light starting strokes and a mitre box for angled ends; shaft holes are drilled with the gear plate clamped flat on a scrap board, never held, with eye protection and a bit matched to the shaft; knives are drawn along a steel rule towards the body with fingers on top of the rule, in light passes, and capped when set down; hot glue is used at its station for quick joints and PVA for the long tower joints, with hot glue on skin cooled under water and never wiped; eye protection is worn when sawing, drilling or near a stretched string. The sheave beam and rope are fitted standing on the floor rather than on a chair, nobody reaches over the running motor or drum or puts fingers near the gears, the motor is tested disengaged, then unloaded, then loaded with one named person holding the switch, loads are increased gradually with nobody under the cage, and loose string is kept on the drum. Bags go under desks, walkways stay clear, one person uses the hot station at a time, hair is tied and sleeves rolled at the saw and drill, every injury is reported, tools are counted back, and the making record is kept from the first cut.

questions.question: Describe how the base and tower faces are built square, how the tower is stood, plumbed and fixed to the base, and how the back-leg and sheave beam are fitted.
questions.expected_answer: The base is a dowel frame or card box checked square with a try square at every corner before and after the glue sets, stiffened with a base plate and marked for the gear plate, with mass added low if planned. The tower faces are built flat over a full-size layout from the working drawing, legs on their lines with nodes marked, each diagonal cut to fit and glued with PVA so every rectangle is triangulated, the face weighted flat and checked square and straight before the glue sets, then left to set fully. Two members hold the faces upright and parallel at the drawn spacing while a third fits the top and bottom cross members with hot glue, then the remaining cross members and the diagonals of the open faces cut to fit; the tower is checked plumb with a square from two sides and corrected before those locking diagonals set, then glued and pinned to the base at its marks. The back-leg is cut to the distance measured on the model between its dimensioned foot and top positions, its ends shaped to bear fully with card gussets; the sheave beam is fitted across the top on the shaft centre line with the sheave turning freely on an axle secured by collars.

questions.question: Explain how the winder is installed and aligned, list the tests in order with what is measured, and show how a failed test is diagnosed, fixed and recorded.
questions.expected_answer: The gear plate is fixed at its mark square to the shaft centre line so the drum's axis is perpendicular to the rope's path to the sheave; the motor is mounted on an adjustable bracket until its pinion meshes and the train turns freely by hand, then fixed; every shaft gets collars; the drum is fitted with its collar and the string tied, wound in the sense that raises the cage, led over the sheave groove and down the centre line to the cage between taut guides; the brake, bumper and depth pointer are fitted. Tests: train turns freely by hand; motor runs the unloaded train with the drum turning the correct direction; lift times for the empty cage and for 100, 200, 300 and 400 grams, noting labouring, skipping or slipping; brake holds 300 grams at mid-shaft; sway at the top in millimetres with 1 kilogram on the platform and the loaded cage hanging; topple test with the cage swung 100 millimetres. Each result enters the evaluation table against its specification with value and verdict; a failure is diagnosed along the flow chart's no branch in order, batteries, friction, drum size, load path, ratio, with each change and its result recorded, for example stalled at 300 grams, drum reduced from 40 to 20 millimetres, now lifts 300 grams in 16 seconds.
